name: Juggler
tagline: Hands-on GUI coding agent with editable session trees
description: Juggler is an open-source GUI coding agent that gives users a visual workbench over everything the LLM does to their codebase. Sessions are stored as Yjs documents rather than chat transcripts, so any point can branch into sub-threads and the entire tree — including approval dialogs waiting on the user — survives quitting and relaunching. The Finder-style Miller-column interface exposes inspectable tool calls, item properties, and raw context, and context items, slash commands, and LLM loop strategies are all JavaScript extensions. It runs as a native desktop app or a headless server that browser clients on any machine can attach to, and it connects to Claude Code, OpenAI, Gemini, Ollama, OpenRouter, and more.
highlights: Session as an editable Yjs tree: branch sub-threads, backtrack, compare, and edit
Persistent sessions that resume exactly, including agent approvals waiting on the user
Everything is a JavaScript extension: context items, slash commands, and LLM loop strategies
Miller-column interface for inspecting tool calls, item properties, and raw context
One session, many clients: native desktop app, browser tabs, and remote machines stay in sync
curatorNote: From the creator of JUCE comes a coding agent that treats the conversation as an inspectable, editable document instead of a doom-scroll transcript. The extension-everything architecture and multi-client desktop/browser model make it a genuinely different take on agent UX.
